item.research_question: What are the underlying causes of thermal instability in charged Ni-rich layered cathode materials, specifically regarding the role of Ni content?
item.material_system: Li0.33Ni0.5+ xCo0.2Mn0.3‐ xO2 (x = 0, 0.1, 0.2), corresponding to NCM523, NCM622, and NCM721
item.processing_route: Synthesis via coprecipitation of NiSO4·7H2O/CoSO4·7H2O/MnSO4·H2O in 1.5 M NaOH at 50 °C (pH 11), followed by drying at 120 °C for 24 h, mixing with LiOH (1.02:1 Li-to-metal ratio), and calcination at 850 °C for 12 h in air; materials were charged to a specific state of charge for thermal testing.
item.test_conditions: In situ synchrotron XRD and HRPD during heating from 25 to 600 °C at 2.5 °C min–1; DSC measurements at 2.5 °C min–1 up to 400 °C; XAS (XANES/EXAFS) collected during heating from 25 to 500 °C.
key_findings: Thermal expansion coefficients for the c hex. lattice parameter were 1.91(2) × 10−5, 1.95(1) × 10−5, and 1.99(2) × 10−5 °C−1 for NCM523, NCM622, and NCM721, respectively, indicating higher Ni content leads to larger thermal expansion.
The onset temperatures for the layered-to-disordered spinel phase transition were 215, 190, and 169 °C for charged NCM523, NCM622, and NCM721, respectively.
The formation temperatures of the M3O4-type spinel phase were 394, 363, and 338 °C for charged NCM523, NCM622, and NCM721, respectively.
The formation temperatures of the rock-salt phase were 440, 414, and 394 °C for charged NCM523, NCM622, and NCM721, respectively.
The change in enthalpy (∆H) during the layered-to-disordered spinel phase transition was –236, –253, and –307 J g–1 for NCM523, NCM622, and NCM721, respectively.
In charged NCM721 at 150 °C, thermal expansion accounted for approximately 80% of the increment in the c hex. lattice parameter, while irreversible structural changes accounted for the remaining 20%.
The Ni─O coordination number dropped to ≈5.5 upon heating to 250 °C, indicating the creation and accumulation of oxygen vacancies around Ni before the phase transition.
Ni ions are reduced starting below the onset temperature of the layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas Co and Mn oxidation states remain relatively stable until higher temperatures.
item.mechanism: Higher Ni content increases the thermal expansion of the Li slab and promotes the formation of oxygen vacancies around Ni ions. These oxygen vacancies and the expanded Li slab lower the energy barrier for cation migration by reducing Pauli repulsion and providing energetically favorable pathways. This facilitates the migration of Ni ions from the transition metal layer to the lithium layer, initiating the layered-to-spinel phase transition and subsequent thermal decomposition.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work, but notes that the findings provide guidance for developing new cathode materials with improved safety characteristics.
quotes: Thermal expansion and oxygen vacancies are proposed as new critical factors that affect the thermal stability of charged Ni‐rich cathode materials
Oxygen vacancies are formed and accumulate mainly around Ni ions until the layered‐to‐spinel phase transition begins.
Thermal expansion and the presence of oxygen vacancies decrease the energy barrier for cation migration and facilitate the phase transitions in charged cathode materials during the heating process.
